description: This seminar focuses on U.S. society and politics during the era of World War II. How did the U.S. mobilize for the war, challenging isolationist currents in American society? How did wartime military and production demands reconfigure gender, race, ethnicity, and class in the U.S., while also reinforcing inequalities? How did global contests between fascism and antifascism shape U.S. politics? How did the war extend or diminish the New Deal? This course examines changes in everyday life in U.S. cities and communities while also paying attention to national politics and structural changes. Working closely with primary and secondary sources, students will practice the craft of history through seminar discussions and research.
shortname: Sem: US Society during World War II
